title: Anthropic Found a Hidden Space Where Claude 'Thinks'
hook: Researchers built a tool that peers inside Claude while it works — and found something like a hidden workspace where the model appears to puzzle over concepts before answering.
key_points: MIT Technology Review reports Anthropic built a tool, the 'Jacobian lens,' to see what's happening inside Claude as it answers or acts.
It's Anthropic's clearest look yet at what a large language model is actually doing internally.
Findings reportedly range from the mundane to the unnerving — not all of it flattering or expected.
This is interpretability research: studying a model's internals, not just its outputs.
It matters because understanding how a model 'thinks' helps explain both its abilities and its failures.
content_html: Large language models are famously hard to inspect — you can see what they output, but not easily how they got there. MIT Technology Review reports that Anthropic has narrowed that gap: researchers built a tool, called the Jacobian lens, that gives the company its clearest view yet into what's actually happening inside Claude while it answers a question or works through a task.
extra_html: This is a research area called interpretability — studying a model's internal machinery rather than just judging it by its output, the same way you might open up an engine instead of only checking if the car starts. What the lens reportedly revealed is a mix: some findings mundane, some described as unnerving, suggesting Claude's internal processing includes patterns researchers didn't fully anticipate. The value of this kind of work isn't a single headline finding — it's the broader payoff of being able to check a model's "reasoning" from the inside, rather than only ever inferring it from what comes out. As models get more capable and get handed more real responsibility (see AI agents), tools like this are part of how the field tries to keep understanding what it's actually built.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'Jacobian lens' that Anthropic built?

choices.text: A tool for examining what's happening inside Claude as it processes a task
A new chatbot feature for customer support
A camera lens used in Anthropic's marketing photos

flashcards.explanation_html: It's a research tool for looking at a model's internal workings — part of the field called interpretability — not a user-facing product feature.

flashcards.prompt: Why does 'interpretability' research matter for everyday AI users?
flashcards.back_html: Understanding what's actually happening inside a model — not just judging it by its answers — helps explain both why it's capable and why it sometimes fails.

flashcards.prompt: Were Anthropic's findings from this tool all reassuring?
flashcards.back_html: No — reporting describes the findings as ranging from mundane to unnerving, meaning some of what researchers saw inside the model wasn't fully expected.
